messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 - high 5xx rate on serving-runtime cluster us-west-2. Alerting #incidents and paging oncall. brief: model-warmup failures + node crash loop, impacting hosted API customers.

sara: seeing the bot — I'm looking at telemetry.

dan: I'm seeing a big spike in model warmup errors starting ~4077776600. Logs show OOM during load and a bunch of deserialization failures.

sara: can you paste the load logs?

dan: here — truncated:
```
[2026-03-15T14:24:12Z] model_load: starting warmup for model rwd/gpt-large-v2
[2026-03-15T14:24:14Z] deser: failed to deserialize tensor blob: unexpected EOF (expected 124M, got 0)
[2026-03-15T14:24:15Z] compile: nvrtc compile timed out after 30s for kernel attention_fused
[2026-03-15T14:24:16Z] runtime: GpuAlloc failed: out of memory (requested 3.8G)
[2026-03-15T14:24:16Z] kernel: oom_kill: Killed process 24321 (python) total-vm:12000000kB, anon-rss:9000000kB
```

mike: I'm oncall. can we confirm node-level OOM or driver crash? please run nvidia-smi and dmesg on the affected node (node-id: compute-uw2-12).

lex: I just pulled node logs — nvidia-smi shows GPUs present but one driver reset happened at 14:24:17. dmesg shows repeated GPU I/O errors and then oom_kill for the python process that was running warmup.

opsbot: deploy-bot: recent model rollout 2026-03-15T13:50:00 -> rwd/gpt-large-v2@v3 is live in us-west-2-canaries.

mike: that aligns — v3 has a larger FFN & we pushed a warmup job that tries to load full-precision weights. looks like simultaneous warmups + compile caused memory pressure.

sara: immediate mitigation options: 1) stop new warmup jobs, 2) rollback traffic to v2 (smaller footprint) for hosted API, 3) route enterprise customer traffic to dedicated fallback pool, 4) drain the affected node and restart driver if necessary.

lex: executing stop of warmup jobs now:
```bash
kubectl -n runtime delete job warmup-rwd-gpt-large-v2-v3 --grace-period=0 --force
```

lex: done, warmup jobs removed.

dan: I also disabled compile cache for that model variant to avoid NVRTC stalls: set model config compile.timeout_ms=10000 and compile.enabled=false for the warmup path.

mike: rolling back traffic to v2 for hosted API (console call):
```json
PATCH /api/v1/routes/serve-hosted
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "model": "rwd/gpt-large-v2@stable" }
```

opsbot: routing change submitted (change-id: rc-9012) — applying.

opsbot: routing change applied; traffic shifted to rwd/gpt-large-v2@stable in us-west-2 (estimated 30s to converge).

sara: while traffic shifts, we should also mark the node as unschedulable and recycle it to clear driver state. mike, can you cordon+drain compute-uw2-12?

mike: cordoning and draining now:
```bash
kubectl cordon compute-uw2-12
kubectl drain compute-uw2-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
ssh ops@compute-uw2-12 'sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm'
```

mike: drain finished, restarting driver. reboot not required yet.

lex: after driver restart, we saw GPU memory cleared and no immediate I/O errors. but one of the pods is CrashLoopBackOff; docker logs show repeated "failed to mmap weights: Invalid argument" then OOM.

dan: those deserialization failures look like truncated artifacts. Could be artifact upload corruption during the v3 rollout. checking artifact storage hashes.

sara: dan, can you verify artifact checksum and re-pull to a healthy node? If corrupt, we should mark artifact as bad and force re-push.

dan: verified — s3 artifact key rwd/gpt-large-v2@v3/weights.bin has a mismatched sha256. re-pushing a fresh copy now.

opsbot: storage-bot: re-upload started (artifact-id: a-5532).

mike: while reupload is in-flight, we should protect customers. Tomas — which customers show elevated errors? any big enterprise impacted?

tomas: customer telemetry: 2 enterprise tenants (AcmeHealth, FinCore) show elevated 5xx and timeouts in last 10m. AcmeHealth hit 80% error rate for a small set of endpoints (ML-assisted triage). I can open an FYI to their SOC.

sara: assign outreach: tomas to contact AcmeHealth support + AE. mike to monitor error rate and escalate if >10%. lex to validate rollback finished. dan to confirm artifact re-upload completion.

mike: monitoring: 5xx rate dropped from 18% to 2% after rollback (current snapshot). good sign.

dan: re-upload finished — artifact checksum now matches and I triggered a manual model load on a canary node with reduced batch/warmup settings:
```yaml
model_variant: rwd/gpt-large-v2@v3
load_config:
  quantize: int8
  disable_warmup: true
  compile:
    enabled: false
  max_batch_tokens: 1024
```
Result: model loaded successfully on canary with int8 quantization and compile disabled.

lex: recommended bridge plan: keep v2 serving for production traffic, mark v3 as quarantined, and create a controlled canary path with quantization+no-compile. We'll re-evaluate compile pipeline separately.

mike: customer impact summary for now: transient 5xx for hosted API customers for ~5–12m; two enterprise tenants had elevated errors but no data loss. outage window: 14:24:00–14:36:00 UTC.

tomas: I've messaged AcmeHealth and FinCore with status + mitigation. Both AEs acknowledged and requested postmortem.

sara: creating incident ticket and assigning follow-ups:
- root cause: model artifact corruption + aggressive warmup + nvrtc compile timeouts leading to GPU memory exhaustion and driver reset
- mitigations applied: stopped warmup jobs, rollback traffic to smaller model, cordoned + restarted node GPU driver, reuploaded artifact, canary load with quantize+no-compile, quarantined v3
- immediate follow-ups: verify artifact integrity pipeline, add post-upload checksum validation, add canary warmup limits (one node at a time), increase compile timeout monitoring and fail open to non-blocking path

opsbot: incident-ticket created (INC-2026-0315-07). owner: sara. severity: P1 -> downgraded to P2 after rollback and error reduction.

mike: handing off to next oncall (lex) at 15:00 UTC. I'll stay reachable for 15 more minutes.

lex: taking oncall handoff. next steps: run regression eval on v3-canary, iterate on compile parameters, and draft postmortem.

sara: thanks all. quick checklist before we close thread: confirm all nodes healthy, ensure no pending warmup jobs, confirm contact with affected customers, and schedule postmortem in 24h.

mike: all nodes healthy, warmup jobs cleared.

dan: re-run artifact full-verify job cron for yesterday night — passed. added extra SHA check in pipeline.

tomas: customers notified.

sara: closing live mitigation. leave thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
